 ![This shot uses a symmetrical 'infinite corridor' to represent the vast capital invested in AI. The Dutch angle adds a subtle sense of instability and 'falling,' paralleling the stock market's downward momentum without being literal.](https://247wallst.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/ai-cloud-crash-puts-coreweave-and-nebius-on-sale-their-next-reports-dec-0d797500-400x211.jpg) 

© 24/7 Wall St.

 

Two of the most closely followed AI cloud providers now trade at roughly half what they fetched a month earlier. From October 6 to November 6, 2026, **CoreWeave** ([NASDAQ:CRWV](https://247wallst.com/companies/CRWV/)) fell 49.9% to $45.89, and **Nebius Group** ([NASDAQ:NBIS](https://247wallst.com/companies/NBIS/) | [NBIS Price Prediction](https://247wallst.com/companies/nbis/price-prediction)) fell 47.7% to $130.78. Both are so-called neoclouds. They buy huge numbers of high-end graphics processors (GPUs), install them in powered data centers, and rent that computing power to AI labs, software companies, trading firms, and enterprises.

Customers pay for short-term capacity or sign multi-year contracts, and the providers borrow money or sell stock to fund the chips and buildings well before the rent comes in. The [post-midterm AI selloff](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/06/stocks-just-had-their-worst-second-day-after-a-midterm-in-nearly-a-century/ "Stocks Just Had Their Worst Second Day After a Midterm in Nearly a Century") that began November 5 hit both stocks on concerns that new state governments will slow the data center buildouts their growth depends on. Each company now faces a dated test: CoreWeave reports on November 10, 2026, and Nebius reports on November 12, 2026. Both are speculative, higher-risk stocks.

## **CoreWeave: Margin Expansion Has to Outrun a Rising Interest Bill**

### What Went Wrong

CoreWeave is down 35.9% year to date and 24.5% from October 29 to November 6. At $45.89, it trades about 66.8% below its 52-week high of $138.25 and well under its 50-day and 200-day moving averages of $78.05 and $90.89. The stock did rebound 5.1% in the November 6 session, but it remains deep in comeback territory.

The political trigger lands hardest on a company that builds at CoreWeave’s pace. On *Bloomberg Businessweek* on November 5, Bloomberg senior editor Eric Weiner said hyperscale growth plans “were based around doing this in Texas, doing this in Ohio. And now there are new governors in those places that are there to block it.” He added, “We were expecting astronomical growth. And now we’re looking at incremental.”

CoreWeave’s specific problem is leverage. Its debt-to-equity ratio is 8.94 and net debt to EBITDA is 10.75. Second quarter interest expense reached $640 million, up from $267 million a year earlier, and the net loss widened to $626 million from $290 million. Free cash flow was −$5.743 billion for the quarter. The company also faces a securities fraud class action alleging it hid data center construction delays. When fresh doubts about how fast new data centers can be built collide with a balance sheet like that, the stock falls hard, which is what happened on November 5. CNBC reported that CoreWeave shares were among the session’s steepest decliners.

### Named Catalyst: Third Quarter Report on November 10

CoreWeave reports after the close on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, with its conference call at 5:00 PM ET. This report matters because management told investors in August that the return from its spending had started. On the second-quarter call, Chief Executive Officer Michael Intrator said, “the operating leverage we have been building” was “beginning to show up clearly in our results.” Adjusted operating income rose to $128 million from $21 million in the prior quarter, and second-quarter GAAP EPS of −$1.14 beat the −$1.447 estimate. That was CoreWeave’s first EPS beat after five straight misses, even though revenue topped estimates in every quarter where one was available (Q2 2025 through Q2 2026).

Intrator also addressed the political risk directly in August, saying moratoriums would affect location rather than demand. Barron’s picked up the same theme on November 5 under the headline “Why Its CEO Isn’t Afraid of Politics.” The November 10 report is the first chance to check that claim against actual numbers.

### What Has to Go Right

* **Revenue inside the guide:** third-quarter revenue of $3.45 billion to $3.6 billion, keeping full-year 2026 revenue of $12.4 billion to $13.2 billion intact.
* **Margin expansion on schedule:** adjusted operating income of $200 million to $260 million, with management still expecting adjusted operating margins to reach the low teens in the fourth quarter.
* **Interest expense inside its range:** the guide calls for $860 million to $940 million. Anything above that range eats directly into the operating leverage story.
* **Backlog converting to revenue:** the backlog stood at $104.2 billion on June 30, and management said more than $25 billion of net new commitments came in during the early weeks of the third quarter. Investors need to see that backlog hold up or grow.
* **Power coming online:** active power was 1.5 gigawatts at quarter-end against a year-end target of more than 1.85 gigawatts, with full-year capital spending guided to $35 billion to $39 billion.

Wall Street remains positive on the name. The consensus price target is $132.18. There is not enough valuation history to say whether the stock is cheap relative to its own past, so the case rests on execution.

### What Would Falsify the Case

The comeback thesis breaks if any of the following show up:

* An EPS miss driven by interest expense above the guided range
* Any new disclosure of construction delays, which would also add weight to the pending class action
* A reduction in the 1.85-gigawatt year-end power target
* A higher capital spending guide without a matching increase in revenue
* Management admitting that state-level opposition is pushing out delivery dates

Any one of these would show the post-midterm selloff was pricing in a genuine problem.

## **Nebius Group: Revenue Has to Catch Up to Guidance That Still Stands**

### What Went Wrong

Nebius is still up 56.2% year to date, from $83.71 at the end of 2025. The recent damage is nonetheless severe. The stock fell 23.9% from October 29 to November 6 and trades about 56.4% below its 52-week high of $299.86. It is also below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages of $206.96 and $177.89, even after an 8.7% rebound on November 6. Shares traded at $208.50 when Nebius filed its second-quarter results in August.

The market-wide question was put simply on CNBC’s *Fast Money* on November 5, in an episode hosted by Melissa Lee, where the panel asked: “Is AI demand just gone or is this getting pushed down the line?” A panelist answered that a delay “means a longer timetable, it means higher costs” and possibly “more friction on the permitting level.”

Nebius’s specific weak points are dilution, concentration, and uneven revenue. In the second quarter, it sold 12.7 million shares through its at-the-market program at a weighted average of $224, raising about $2.8 billion, and it had 12.3 million shares left under that program. Its convertible debt has a book value of $8.5 billion against a fair value of $20.8 billion, a gap that points to more future share dilution. Three customers made up 24%, 21%, and 14% of second-quarter revenue. Revenue also missed consensus in Q3 2025 and Q4 2025 before beating in the first two quarters of 2026. Local politics already touches Nebius directly: a public hearing on its Vineland, New Jersey, project adjourned without a vote, although management said the switch to on-site fuel cells would have “no significant impact expected on the project timeline.”

### Named Catalyst: Third-Quarter Report on November 12

Nebius reports before the market opens on Thursday, November 12, 2026, with a conference call at 8:00 AM ET. The report matters because Nebius reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $3 billion to $3.4 billion after first-half revenue of $399 million and $582.3 million. That means the second half has to produce about $2.02 billion just to reach the low end, and roughly $2.42 billion to reach the top. Consensus for the third quarter is about $904.8 million in revenue and EPS of −$1.238.

Management said capacity deployed late in the second quarter would begin contributing to revenue in Q3, and warned that “There is a gap between the connected power and the revenues coming.” CEO Arkady Volozh described the demand picture without hedging: “The demand for what we are building continues to be enormous, and we have the right business model to capture it.”

### What Has to Go Right

* **Revenue in line or ahead:** a result at or above the roughly $904.8 million consensus, with the $3 billion to $3.4 billion full-year guide reaffirmed.
* **A visible path on annualized revenue:** the annualized run rate was $3 billion at the end of June against a year-end target of $7 billion to $9 billion. The September exit rate needs to show real progress toward that target.
* **Margins holding:** group adjusted EBITDA margin was 41% in the second quarter, against a full-year target of about 40%.
* **Capacity and funding on track:** 800 megawatts to 1 gigawatt of connected power in 2026, the 5 gigawatt contracted power target, and the expected more than $9 billion of customer prepayments in 2026 helping fund a capital spending guide of $20 billion to $25 billion.
* **A wider customer base:** the four second-quarter deals with Reflection, Cohere, a U.S. neolab, and a quant-trading firm averaged more than $1 billion each. The concentration figures need to start coming down.

The consensus price target is $281, with more Buy ratings than Hold or Sell ratings. The stock trades at a price-to-sales ratio of 26.52 on trailing revenue. That number reflects expected growth, and no multi-year valuation history is available to show the stock is cheap against its own past.

### What Would Falsify the Case

A revenue miss on November 12 would be the third in five quarters and would undercut the full-year guide. A cut to the 2026 revenue guide or the $7 billion to $9 billion annualized revenue target, a smaller connected-power goal, a new delay at Vineland, larger stock sales through the at-the-market program without faster revenue growth, or a bigger share of revenue from its top three customers would each mean the selloff was right to mark the stock down.

## **Verdict: Nebius Has the Clearer Path, CoreWeave Has the Tighter Margin for Error**

Nebius enters its report in better shape. It had $8 billion in cash at June 30, and its test comes down to turning capacity it has already built into revenue. CoreWeave’s comeback depends on reaching a narrow window: adjusted operating income of $200 million to $260 million while interest costs rise toward $940 million, and a miss on either line would confirm the concerns about its debt load. On the evidence available ahead of the November 10 and November 12 reports, Nebius has the stronger comeback case, while CoreWeave’s case holds up only if its third quarter shows the margin expansion arriving on schedule.

**Nebius Group N.V.** NBIS will report third-quarter 2026 results on Thursday, before market open.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for loss for the to-be-reported quarter is pegged at 61 cents. Analysts have revised their estimates upward for NBIS' bottom line over the past 60 days. The consensus estimate for total revenues is pinned at $916.78 million.

## What Our Model Predicts for NBIS

The combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy), or 3 (Hold) increases the chances of an earnings beat. That is the case here. ## Factors to Note Ahead of NBIS' Q3 Earnings

Strong demand for AI cloud infrastructure, increased capacity utilization and continued infrastructure expansion are expected to have supported Nebius Group's third-quarter 2026 performance. On the last earnings call, management highlighted that demand continued to exceed available supply, with the company selling out capacity as quickly as it came online. Second-quarter revenues surged 454% year over year to $582 million, driven by capacity added in the first quarter, improved infrastructure efficiency and contributions from new businesses. Management expects capacity deployed late in the second quarter to begin contributing to third-quarter revenues, potentially supporting sequential growth.

Favorable GPU pricing trends could have further supported third-quarter performance. Management highlighted that AI compute pricing continued to strengthen amid robust demand. Nebius launched its first capacity auction, which cleared at a price 15% above its previous highest Blackwell-generation pricing and 20% above its existing pipeline pricing. The company also identified opportunities for shorter-duration capacity contracts, typically lasting three to six months, commanding $40 million to $50 million per megawatt or more. These premium arrangements could have supported monetization opportunities, although management indicated that newly secured deals would largely begin contributing from late 2026 onward.

Capacity expansion is expected to have remained a key factor influencing third-quarter revenues. Nebius reaffirmed its target of achieving 800 megawatts to 1 gigawatt of connected power by year-end 2026 and raised its contracted power target to 5 gigawatts. However, management noted that newly connected capacity requires data center commissioning, network construction, GPU cluster deployment and customer onboarding before generating revenues. This process can take several months, potentially limiting immediate revenue contributions despite accelerated infrastructure development.

Customer demand and contract momentum could have strengthened the company's business outlook. During the second quarter, Nebius secured four major AI cloud contracts averaging more than $1 billion each, including agreements with Reflection and Cohere. These contracts offer yields of $20 million to $25 million per megawatt, with upfront payments covering 50% to 60% of associated capital expenditures. However, management expects these agreements to begin generating revenues from late fourth-quarter 2026 onward, limiting their direct impact on third-quarter results.

Growing contributions from Token Factory, inference services, acquisitions and the asset-light business model might have supported revenues and profitability. These businesses contributed to second-quarter adjusted EBITDA margin expansion to 41% from 32% sequentially. Higher utilization and high-margin services are likely to have supported third-quarter margins. However, continued growth investments and the timing of capacity deployment remained potential profitability headwinds.

[![Zacks Investment Research](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///ywAAAAAAQABAAACAUwAOw==)](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/4e96cd854cec810a14ae707fe4a67c9dd80d4373ef3849027c3b223b4d037955/lightyear_networkapi/resizefit_w960%3Bquality_80%3Bformat_webp/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fzacks.com%2F6e78d46db6dc8707c23042a2fbcea1f7.jpg)

Zacks Investment Research

 

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Substantial capital expenditure requirements and infrastructure execution risks could also have weighed on performance. Nebius incurred approximately $5.7 billion in capital expenditures during the second quarter, primarily for GPUs and data center expansion. Additionally, pending site-layout approval at its Vineland project remained a potential execution risk, although management did not anticipate significant timeline disruptions.

Nebius reaffirmed its 2026 revenue guidance of $3 billion to $3.4 billion, annualized run-rate revenue of $7 billion to $9 billion, adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 40% and capital expenditures of $20 billion to $25 billion. No specific third-quarter guidance was provided. Overall, third-quarter results are expected to reflect strong AI infrastructure demand, favorable pricing and capacity additions, partly offset by heavy investments and infrastructure deployment-related timing challenges.

## Key Developments

On Oct. 21, 2026, Nebius introduced publicly available, live spot pricing for GPU compute, offering AI developers greater transparency and flexibility in managing infrastructure costs. The company also highlighted reserve auctions, pay-as-you-go pricing and a pilot capacity-rebate program. Also, Nebius announced the addition of agentic workflows to its Physical AI Workbench in collaboration with NVIDIA. The open-source framework integrates data generation, simulation, training and evaluation for robotics development.

On Oct. 19, 2026, Nebius expanded its AI Builder Program in Europe with a $10 million commitment to support developers through compute grants, potential funding opportunities and community programs. Working alongside NVIDIA, Accel and European venture capital firms, the initiative aims to help developers build and scale open-source AI technologies and businesses.

On Oct. 1, 2026, Nebius acquired Inferize, an inference optimization company, to strengthen its Nebius Token Factory platform. Inferize's technology reduces the time required to launch and scale large AI models, helping improve GPU utilization, infrastructure efficiency and token economics. Its engineering team and technology have joined Nebius's managed inference operations.

On Sept. 22, 2026, Nebius introduced dynamic spot pricing for preemptible virtual machines (PVMs), allowing GPU compute prices to adjust automatically based on available capacity and real-time demand. The pricing mechanism offers customers greater flexibility and cost savings for non-critical workloads, including data processing, experimentation and short-term model fine-tuning.

On Sept. 10, 2026, Nebius launched its AI Builder Program to help developers build and scale AI systems using open models and independent infrastructure. The initiative provides access to credits, technical resources, educational courses, certifications, expert guidance and a developer community. It aims to help AI builders maintain greater control over their models, tools and technology stacks.

On Sept. 8, 2026, Nebius announced a partnership with Palantir to provide sovereign AI infrastructure to Palantir's commercial customers. Under the agreement, Palantir named Nebius its preferred sovereign AI infrastructure partner and plans to integrate Nebius compute and inference capabilities within its enterprise environment following an integration period.

Nebius shares have lost 30.4% over the past year, underperforming the Zacks Computer & Technology sector's decline of 10.6% and the Zacks Internet Software Services industry's growth of 1.1%. The S&P 500 Composite has declined 2.3% over the same time frame.

In comparison, NVDA, MSFT and CRWV trade at multiples of 19.64X, 8.38X and 4.24X, respectively.

## What to Do With NBIS Stock Before Q3 Earnings?

Despite near-term profitability pressures from heavy infrastructure investments, Nebius' robust AI cloud demand, expanding capacity and favorable GPU pricing trends strengthen its growth prospects.

Investors can consider buying NBIS stock ahead of its third-quarter 2026 earnings release, supported by the likelihood of an earnings beat and strong long-term AI infrastructure growth opportunities.

# When does Nebius report earnings? Thursday before the bell, with the call at 8 a.m. ET: what to watch

Nebius posts its third-quarter results before the US market opens Thursday, November 12. Here are the targets it set in August and the numbers investors will check first.

By Nacionale News

·

5 min read

Photo: Luca Marfè at Italia all'ONU / [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:NASDAQ_Market_Site_201506.jpg) · CC BY 2.0

Nebius Group reports its third-quarter results before the US stock market opens on Thursday, November 12, and holds a conference call at 8 a.m. ET (5 a.m. PT) the same morning, [the company said](https://nebius.com/newsroom/nebius-group-announces-date-of-third-quarter-2026-results-and-conference-call) on October 30. The webcast and its replay are reached through a registration link on Nebius’s [investor hub](https://nebius.com/investor-hub).

The timing matters because NBIS shares have already moved on someone else’s numbers. They jumped on Wednesday after CoreWeave’s results lifted AI cloud stocks, as we explained in [why Nebius stock rose a day before its report](https://www.nacionale.com/en/articles/why-is-nebius-stock-up-today-nbis-coreweave-earnings-november-11-q3-results-thursday). Thursday is when Nebius has to show its own figures. Below is what it promised in August and what analysts say they will be checking. None of this is investment advice.

### What Nebius promised for 2026

When it reported its second quarter on August 12, Nebius kept its full-year targets unchanged, according to [MarketBeat’s summary of the call](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/nebius-group-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-12/):

* Revenue of $3.0 billion to $3.4 billion for 2026.
* Annualized run-rate revenue (ARR) of $7 billion to $9 billion by year end. ARR is the latest month’s revenue multiplied by 12, a measure of how fast the business is running at a given moment.
* Capital spending of $20 billion to $25 billion this year.
* An adjusted EBITDA margin of about 40% for the group. Adjusted EBITDA is profit before interest, tax, depreciation and some other costs, so it leaves out the large depreciation charges on GPUs.

At the end of June, ARR stood at $3 billion, up from $1.9 billion at the end of March, [MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/nebius-group-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-12/) and [Trending Topics](https://www.trendingtopics.eu/nebius-neoclouds-revenue-jumps-454-yoy-stock-rises-16/) both reported. That leaves a long way to go to reach $7 billion to $9 billion by December, so Thursday’s ARR figure is the clearest progress check. Nebius said it would give formal 2027 guidance later this year, [according to MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/nebius-group-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-12/), and it is not yet known whether that comes on Thursday.

### What analysts expect for the quarter

The consensus compiled by [Earnings Whispers](https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/NBIS/22887) on November 4 is revenue of about $916.8 million and a loss of $0.61 a share. That compares with $146.1 million in revenue a year earlier, and with $582.3 million and a $0.12 loss per share in the second quarter. Other data providers publish somewhat different figures, so a reported beat or miss can depend on which estimate a headline uses.

The Q2 figures appear in the company’s [results table, republished by StorageNewsletter](https://www.storagenewsletter.com/2026/08/20/nebius-fiscal-2q26-financial-results/), which also shows a net loss from continuing operations of $190.4 million for that quarter.

### The revenue arithmetic

Revenue in the first half of 2026 was about $981 million, [Earnings Whispers](https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/NBIS/22887) noted. If the third quarter lands near the $917 million consensus, the fourth quarter would need about $1.1 billion for Nebius to reach the bottom of its range and about $1.5 billion to reach the top. That is our arithmetic from the guidance and the consensus, not a company forecast.

That is why analysts will listen closely to how management describes the year. In August, Nebius management said the newer agreements would come online later in 2026 and were not expected to materially affect this year’s revenue guidance, but should contribute to 2027 and beyond, [MarketBeat reported](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/nebius-group-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-12/). The full-year consensus of about $3.48 billion is already above the top of Nebius’s range, [Earnings Whispers said](https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/NBIS/22887), so keeping the range unchanged rather than raising it could disappoint some investors.

### Five things investors will check

* **The big contracts.** Nebius signed four AI cloud contracts in the second quarter, each averaging more than $1 billion, [Trending Topics reported](https://www.trendingtopics.eu/nebius-neoclouds-revenue-jumps-454-yoy-stock-rises-16/). [Earnings Whispers](https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/NBIS/22887) names Reflection and Cohere among the customers. The question is whether that capacity is coming online on schedule.
* **Power and data centers.** Nebius raised its target for contracted power to 5 gigawatts by year end, with 800 megawatts to 1 gigawatt expected to be connected by the end of 2026, [MarketBeat reported](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/nebius-group-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-12/). Its executives also said connected power takes several months to turn into revenue. Any delay at sites such as Vineland, New Jersey, would matter, [Earnings Whispers noted](https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/NBIS/22887).
* **Margins.** Group adjusted EBITDA margin was 41% in the second quarter, [per MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/nebius-group-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-12/). Holding it near that level while spending heavily is a test of pricing.
* **Customer prepayments.** Nebius expects more than $9 billion in prepayments from customers this year, which helps pay for new capacity, [Trending Topics](https://www.trendingtopics.eu/nebius-neoclouds-revenue-jumps-454-yoy-stock-rises-16/) and [MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/nebius-group-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-12/) reported. An update shows how much of the build-out customers are funding.
* **Borrowing and new shares.** Losses per share and dilution both depend on how the spending is financed. That is covered below.

### How Nebius is paying for the build-out

Since the last report, Nebius has raised large amounts of new money. In August it closed a sale of $5.75 billion of convertible notes in two parts: $3.45 billion due 2030 at 0.50% interest and $2.3 billion due 2034 at 4.50%, [the company said](https://nebius.com/newsroom/nebius-group-announces-closing-of-private-offering-of-convertible-senior-notes-with-aggregate-gross-proceeds-of-approximately-5-75-billion). Convertible notes can later be turned into shares. On October 22 it announced a $3.5 billion secured facility from Citi with a 364-day term, priced at SOFR plus 2.75% at the start and up to 3.50%, [according to its release](https://nebius.com/newsroom/nebius-secures-3-5-billion-financing-facility-with-citi).

In the second quarter it also sold about $2.8 billion of new shares at an average of about $224, [Trending Topics reported](https://www.trendingtopics.eu/nebius-neoclouds-revenue-jumps-454-yoy-stock-rises-16/). With the stock well below that price, [Earnings Whispers noted](https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/NBIS/22887) that any further share sales would dilute existing holders more. Worries about heavy borrowing for data centers were one reason AI cloud stocks had sold off before CoreWeave’s report, as our [piece on the CoreWeave results](https://www.nacionale.com/en/articles/crwv-stock-coreweave-q3-earnings-beat-raised-2026-outlook-after-hours) explains.

### What we don’t know

* Whether Nebius will raise, keep or cut its 2026 targets, and whether 2027 guidance comes on Thursday.
* How the stock will react. It can move sharply before the 9:30 a.m. ET open, because the results come out before the market opens.
* Which consensus figure each outlet will use to call the quarter a beat or a miss.
